subject: s.d. of redundant parameter with contr.sum

messages.author: 3174a012d5336ba2
messages.subject: s.d. of redundant parameter with contr.sum
parts:
Hi,

Apologies if this is too obvious a question (especially after the recent
"Plot marginals for interaction effects" in the forum).

Suppose I have a model that I have fitted after setting contrasts to
contr.sum. Now, for some factors/factor combinations I want to obtain
the standard deviation of the coefficient for the last level of a factor/factor combination
(the redundant one, which is -sum(all the others)). I think I really only have two options:

- refit the model changing which is the last level of the factor(s)

- use inla.make.lincombs (which amounts to fitting the models again :-( ),
  as explained in the FAQ (q. 17)


Recoding the factor levels is simple, but the models take a long time to
run. So I was wondering if there is any shortcut, but I do not see it.

Thanks,

R.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] s.d. of redundant parameter with contr.sum
parts:
Quick comment:
You shouldn't have to rerun the entire fitting if all you need is to add lincombs; you just need to supply your existing output to give inla() the parameter mode, and set restart=FALSE. That way, only the integration (including the lincombs) step needs to be rerun, and not the optimization step.
I believe this is mentioned in more detail somewhere in the FAQ.

Finn L
